body.objective: Extend the landed Groebner and semialgebraic layers with proof-carrying algebraic component and singularity analysis. The immediate consumers are sf:program/work/bridge-global-bounded-cone-real-zero-locus, sf:program/work/bridge-component-incidence-classification and the residual-atlas cone overlays. Conflux can find repeated rank and incidence patterns, but it cannot presently prove whether two apparent branches are distinct irreducible components, embedded components, intersections, singular strata or presentation artifacts.
body.stop_condition: For bounded-variable polynomial ideals over Q and declared algebraic extensions, provide saturation and colon ideals, radicals where decidable, equidimensional and primary decomposition for a declared certified class, irreducible-component witnesses, ideal intersection and inclusion, Jacobian singular loci, tangent spaces and tangent cones, multiplicity or local-dimension data, normalization only for a tightly declared low-dimensional class, and real-component filtering through the semialgebraic layer. Every decomposition must reconstruct the source ideal up to the exact declared equivalence and carry membership/nonmembership witnesses. Reproduce one existing Paper-13 multi-branch bounded cone, its component-incidence graph and singular intersection, with an independent msolve/Singular/Sage rail. Export canonical component and incidence objects to Conflux.
body.forbid: no numerical irreducible decomposition promoted to exact; no radical equality inferred from matching sampled zeros; no generic component decomposition that silently drops embedded or exceptional parameter components; no claim of complete normalization outside the declared algorithmic class; no physics-specific branch equations in lib/math; no Conflux merge without ideal-containment witnesses
notes: Priority A. This turns the residual atlas from a table of solved fixtures into a canonical geometry of branches and intersections.
The first release may target zero-dimensional and low-dimensional rational ideals with explicit UNDECIDED outside its certified scope.
